contents.contents: Arranged in seven memre, and each memra is comprised of 100 sayings; the first two memre are lost, and the text begins in the middle of the third memra
contents.notes: The author is, in various places, called Shemʻun the persecuted or Shemʻun the solitary, and in some places these titles are combined (ܫܡܥܘܢ ܪܕܝܦܐ ܝܚܝܕܝܐ); a note on fol. 113v seems to identify him as a student of ܡܪܝ ܘܐܒܘܢ ܘܪܒܢ ܝܫܘܥ (Rabban Ishoʻ); see Baumstark, Geschichte der syrischen Literatur , p. 210
